historical_reviews.deepseek: Does not assess the functional RTC/IO path or forced-driver conflict.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds ownership warning but lacks device/register semantics and component-by-component coverage.
historical_reviews.related_cases: This is distinct from mux and FPGA paths: timekeeping integrity and possible kernel RTC binding make forced access uniquely risky, and a second IO-expander endpoint may require separate evidence.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Use owner-approved read-only device-specific checks for RTC identity/time progression and IO-expander identity/status, preferably without `-f`; preserve clock and GPIO state.

original_test_intent: Verify BMC I2C-5 can communicate with the RTC and IO expander while preserving system timekeeping and IO state, with separate evidence for each named endpoint.
original_method: Prove logical BMC I2C-5 maps to Linux bus4; identify RTC and IO-expander addresses from PID1114953; inspect kernel/daemon ownership; read safe identity/status/time registers through the supported driver or approved raw path; validate RTC time progresses against a reference and IO-expander state matches the non-mutating oracle; avoid broad scans and forced access where possible; confirm no clock/GPIO changes.
manual_activity: BMC/platform owner provides bus numbering, RTC and IO-expander identities/registers, driver-safe access and recovery; physical probing/photos are not inferred.
required_inputs: PID1114953 mapping from BMC I2C-5 to Linux bus4 and both RTC/IO-expander endpoints
Device identity at0x6f and authoritative meaning/access mode of register0x0b
Separate IO-expander address, safe identity/input-status register and expected value/mask if0x6f is the RTC
RTC expected format, clock source, reference/tolerance and read consistency/progression rules
Kernel RTC and GPIO/IO-expander driver ownership plus approved sysfs/driver interface or raw-access exception
Timeout/NACK/error criteria, clock/GPIO preservation and recovery
safety_requirements: Prefer kernel/driver read interfaces; do not use `-f` while a bound driver owns0x6f absent explicit platform approval
Do not scan arbitrary bus4 addresses with quick-write discovery
Confirm register0x0b is read-safe and no pointer/read side effect clears flags or latches
Do not set time, alarms or IO directions/outputs; capture clock and GPIO state before/after
Abort on time jump, driver error, unexpected IO change, NACK, timeout, stuck bus or BMC degradation
agent_execution_scope: Collect controller mapping, device/driver ownership, reference time and IO baseline
After approval, perform separate safe RTC and IO-expander read-only checks and verify state preservation
Do not probe/solder, force bound devices by default, scan blindly, set time/alarm/GPIO, reset BMC, auto-retry or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve bus mapping and endpoint identities
Define RTC register/time oracle and IO-expander register/value oracle
Approve driver interface or exceptional forced raw access and recovery
Review separate RTC/IO evidence plus state preservation and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Incorrect physical-only substitution; the source gives a functional BMC query.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Do not run `i2cdetect -q` or `-f` by default. After ownership/protocol approval, retain `i2ctransfer -f -y 4 w1@0x6f 0x0b r1` only if no safe driver interface exists, and add the PID-defined separate non-mutating IO-expander check; capture time/GPIO state before and after.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC bus4, address0x6f, register0x0b, r1, BMC I2C-5, RTC, IO expander, PID1114953 and 15/5-minute scope are preserved as source facts.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use driver-safe read-only checks for RTC identity/time progression and IO-expander identity/status, resorting to the forced raw read only under owner control.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds separate coverage for both endpoints, clock/GPIO preservation and driver ownership while rejecting invented physical probing and unsafe broad scanning.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One byte from0x6f cannot prove both RTC and IO-expander connectivity without documented proxy/multi-function semantics; RTC reachability also needs credible time progression rather than an arbitrary register value.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Forced access can race the RTC driver or affect time/alarm flags; reading IO registers may involve latches on some devices, so the exact vendor protocol is required.

project_override_considerations: Wistron I2C policy requires BMC controller/bus, every target address, expected response and recovery. Kernel ownership is especially relevant for the RTC and IO-expander GPIO state.
expected_evidence: PID map for BMC I2C-5/bus4 and both RTC/IO-expander endpoints
BMC identity, RTC/IO device IDs, kernel driver bindings and access-owner baseline
Vendor definitions for0x6f register0x0b and separate IO-expander safe register
Timestamped RTC raw/decoded values across an interval versus reference with tolerance
Timestamped IO-expander expected-versus-observed status/value without direction/output change
Pre/post clock, alarms, GPIO, bus/BMC health and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source maps logical I2C-5 to bus4 without proof, provides only one forced0x6f/register0x0b byte for two named devices, and defines no expected value. DeepSeek/GPT V2 add physical probing absent from the Procedure.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The connectivity purpose is clear and both endpoints can be validated after owner-supplied mapping/register contracts; it is RPUC, not Manual Only or BLOCKED.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row136 Wistron-HW Robust-00014-V002: provide PID1114953 mapping from BMC I2C-5 to bus4, identify0x6f/register0x0b and define its expected byte/read side effects, plus the separate IO-expander address/register/value oracle. Define RTC time format/reference/tolerance, kernel driver ownership and whether `-f` is permitted, safe scan policy, timeout/NACK criteria, clock/GPIO preservation and recovery; confirm physical probing is not mandatory unless separately scoped.

review_improvement: Restores functional automation, separates RTC from IO-expander coverage and treats forced kernel-driver bypass/timekeeping integrity as the case-specific safety boundary.
independent_technical_reasoning: The test names two endpoints but supplies only one read. Unless PID shows0x6f is a proxy or combined device, the command cannot cover the IO expander. Because RTC devices are commonly driver-owned and stateful, `-f` is more consequential than an ordinary read: the review must prefer supported interfaces, prove register semantics and verify clock/alarm state did not change. Functional evidence—not invented probing—can validate both paths once each oracle is defined.
